name_en: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
canonical_claim: For every positive modulus and every residue class coprime to that modulus, there are infinitely many prime natural numbers in that residue class.
domain_and_universes: Natural-number modulus q with positivity/nonzero condition; a reduced residue class represented either by a : ZMod q with IsUnit a or by an integer/natural coprimality condition. Exact encoding is open for the statement gate.
quantifiers: a : reduced residue class modulo q
unbounded prime p in that residue class
hypotheses: q is positive (or an equivalent nonzero-modulus condition)
a is coprime to q (or is a unit of ZMod q)
conclusion: The primes congruent to a modulo q form an infinite set; equivalently, above every natural bound there is such a prime.

alternate_encodings.target: infinitude of the set of primes in the residue class
for every bound n there exists a prime p > n in the residue class

excluded_degenerate_cases: The statement phase must fix q = 0 and q = 1 behavior, the representative of a residue class, and whether primality is over Nat or Int. Non-coprime classes are excluded from the theorem rather than treated as a conclusion-bearing case.
